question.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=-x(t)+y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=-x(t)-3y(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear differential equations above. The eigenvector $\mathbf{v} = [1, \ -1]^T$ corresponds to the repeated eigenvalue $\lambda=-2$ of the system's matrix $A.$ The vector $\mathbf{w} = [0, \ 1]^T$ is such that $(A - \lambda I)\mathbf{w}= \mathbf{v}.$ Sketch the phase portrait of the linear system above.
question.worked_solution:
Since we have a repeated eigenvalue $\lambda=-2$ (of multiplicity two) and only one corresponding eigenvector $\mathbf{v},$ the solution of the system is given by

$$
\mathbf{x}(t) = c_1\mathbf{v} e^{\lambda t}  + c_2 (\mathbf{v}  te^{\lambda t}  +  \mathbf{w}e^{\lambda t} \, ),
$$

where $\mathbf{w}$ is a solution to the equation $(A - \lambda I)\mathbf{w}= \mathbf{v}.$

In our case, 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14124655/assets/72cfb513575d6481a4ee3206ff4d74568dc8397e10fec34ae89242a444a6b2d2.svg) 
Thus, the general solution of the system is

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}] & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-2t}+{c}_{2}([\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]t{e}^{-2t}+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-2t}) \\  & ={c}_{1}{e}^{-2t}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}{e}^{-2t}[\begin{aligned}t \\ -t+1\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.\end{aligned}
$$

The line that passes through the origin and is parallel to ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14124655/assets/461a22d18752e55eada19b3f0bb58be61bee7a9cd88437304f291c4a9992bdae.svg) has the equation 

$$
y= -x
$$

and the straight-line solutions of the form
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14124655/assets/ed2fb464c555b2cbf0ffa7f67084e5565fc7c9e80e0263647e1303f69a91895d.svg)
lie on that line. 

Since $e^{-2t} \to 0$ as $t \to \infty,$ these solutions approach the origin as $t \to \infty.$

Let's add the solutions to the phase space.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14124655/assets/523dccf73169d02b6bdf4297e96ec84bcc6c43213cdd722000f3a987a534b218.png)

Now, consider solutions of the form
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14124655/assets/0589d1749aed66b91a94b49e4a8815bc4a8621eef3b45e535d2117e81d4f416d.svg)
When $c_2=1,$ we get the following curve:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=t{e}^{-2t} \\ y=(-t+1){e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Computing the coordinates (rounded to two decimal places) of several points on the curve, we get the table below.

| $t$ | $-0.5$ | $0$ | $0.5$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x$ | $-1.36$ | $0$ | $0.18$ |
| $y$ | $4.08$ | $1$ | $0.18$ |

Let's add the solutions to the phase space.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14124655/assets/dbf5a13ecd5e81c399204fd29d235e410fcb62274555cf3e5b32a383c1078d24.png)

The phase portrait of our system looks as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14124655/assets/6c84cd04f3b037bee48d02d3183114e2668fbbd110bd44e9311e7ff454db8bac.png)
